newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kia - Europe business unhurt by bail-out.
newsitem.headline: Kia - Europe business unhurt by bail-out.

text.p: The German unit of struggling South Korean car maker Kia Motors Corp said on Thursday German and European business was not being hurt by the parent company's financial turmoil.
So far this year Kia has exported 28,656 cars to Europe, putting sales just ahead of the pace last year, when it exported 53,331 cars to Europe.
Kia Motors Deutschland GmbH has sold about 7,000 cars in the first half of 1997, after selling just over 15,000 in all of 1996, a spokesman told Reuters.
"There is financial difficulty at the mother company, but it is not having an impact on Europe or Germany," said T.S. Chung, Kia president for Europe, in a statement.
Kia Motors Deutschland was unaffected by the group's massive bail-out plan because it operates as independent business, the spokesman said.
"Of course there are connections, but financially we have our own base here," the spokesman said. "We are not dependent on Korean banks. We depend on German and European banks."

Debt-riddled Kia Motors was forced recently into an emergency reorganisation backed by bail-out loans from its banking partners, and planned to shed half its 28 domestic affiliates, sell other assets and slash its workforce.
It blamed the disaster on a recession in the Korean car market and losses by subsidiaries such as Kia Steel, and a hostile takeover attempt by the Samsung Group, a major South Korean conglomerate.
